text:
ajay: quick sketch — we need a short playbook for geo-fanout coordination to avoid cross-region latency spikes and accidental residency breaches. thinking: a small coordinator stage that tags requests and enforces locality + soft-fallbacks.

olivia: +1. can you outline constraints? e.g., when do we fanout vs route single-region?

ajay: rough constraints: 1) if tenant has resident-region tag -> route primary only. 2) if request crosses PII/consent boundary -> block fanout. 3) if model/variant not available -> consider regional fallback or degraded model. keep decisions cheap.

kevin: important: avoid thundering herd during regional failover. coordinator should do randomized drip + circuit-breaker per-tenant. also want backpressure signal to upstream proxies.

maya: agree re: backpressure. also we should record a "fanout_trace" header for observability and postmortem. simple format: 
```
Fanout-Trace: r=region-A;t=tenant-123;policy=resident-allow;seq=4
```

sam: curious about data residency enforcement: does coordinator enforce by dropping or by proxying to a local policy service?

ajay: plan A: coordinator consults a local policy cache (eventually-consistent) and enforces. if cache miss -> sync call to policy service with 50ms timeout -> default to safe (no cross-region) on timeout.

olivia: that sounds conservative but OK. we should list failure modes: 1) stale cache -> accidentally allow cross-region, 2) timeout -> unnecessary reject, 3) cascade during control-plane outage.

kevin: propose mitigation: prefer explicit allow list for high-volume tenants. and add a transient override token for emergency ops (audited).

infra-bot: deploy: canary of geo-fanout-coordinator v0.1 started on canary cluster eu-west-1 at 1765433300.

maya: ops question — how do callers express fanout preference? header or param? would like both: header for proxies, param for SDKs. e.g. `X-Fanout-Mode: prefer-local|allow-fanout|force-fanout`

sam: logging: must capture which region served the final response and which were tried. also add a token-level cost estimate so Optimize can tune batching/quantization.

ajay: next steps: i'll drop a tiny proto RFC in docs (link: https://redwood-internal/notes/geo-fanout-playbook) with sequence diagrams, failure matrix, and a minimal API: 
```
POST /v1/infer
Headers: X-Fanout-Mode, Fanout-Trace
Coordinator response: 200 + {served_region, fallback_regions[], model_variant}
```

olivia: can you include TTL semantics for policy cache + how we invalidate on tenant changes?

ajay: yes — default TTL 60s for policy cache, invalidation webhook from control plane on explicit change. will add to RFC.

kevin: also add an operator runbook for noisy failovers: steps to reduce fanout volume and to toggle emergency override.

maya: sounds good. i'll pair with you to prototype the trace header and the log format.

sam: +1. i'll add a quick test harness to simulate downstream consent rejection so we can validate rollback behavior.

ajay: thanks all — i'll post the proto RFC by EOD and tag arch for review. :thumbsup:
